title: rollout-gate-latch-traffic-leak-and-version-unpinning-action-items
creator: Ava Martinez
summary: During an automated rollout gate evaluation, a gating latch mis-evaluated region-specific routing rules which allowed significant traffic to flow to an incompatible model variant. The mismatch caused increased error rates, KV-cache deserialization failures for pinned clients, and a failed rollback due to pinned-version conflicts. This doc captures the immediate mitigations, root cause analysis, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 14:12 UTC - Rollout job started: canary gate for model v2026-03-09a initiated for 10% global traffic with region overrides.
14:17 UTC - Health probes from eu-west-1 began reporting elevated 500s for requests hitting the new variant (manifest mismatch).
14:23 UTC - Observability alert: error-rate > 5% on model/v2026-03-09a in eu-west-1. On-call paged.
14:35 UTC - Ops attempted automated rollback; rollout controller returned PINLOCK error preventing immediate rollback for a subset of sessions pinned to the variant.
15:05 UTC - Engineers discovered routing gate logic applied a stale region override config that flipped traffic fraction to 65% in eu-west-1 (ops race with config push).
15:40 UTC - Team disabled regional override via emergency config, reducing traffic to 5% while investigation continued.
16:10 UTC - KV-cache deserialization errors traced to model signature change; some clients still pinned to pre-rollout cache format causing malformed KV entries.
17:00 UTC - Manual intervention: a controlled unpinning of new sessions and graceful draining of affected workers performed; overall traffic normalized.
18:45 UTC - Incident declared mitigated; monitoring entered 48h high watch period.
root_cause: A race between a config push (region override table) and the rollout controller caused the gate evaluation to use a stale override that assigned an incorrect traffic fraction for eu-west-1. The new model variant introduced a minor change to KV cache serialization that was not compatible with clients pinned to the old serialization format. The controller's pinlock logic prevented an immediate rollback for active pinned sessions, complicating remediation and prolonging elevated errors.
detection: Service-level SLO alerting in the observability pipeline detected error-rate increases and latency spikes. Automated canary health checks flagged the model but the gate evaluation logs were not surfaced in the initial alert runbook, delaying pinpointing region-specific overrides by ~18 minutes.
immediate_remediations: Disabled eu-west-1 override in config store to restore intended 10% traffic fraction (ops).
Performed targeted unpin of new sessions for affected customer subset to allow rollback where safe (runtime team).
Added an emergency SaaS guard that rejects rollout if controller-config checksum mismatch detected (temporary hotfix PR merged).
Opened high-watch channel and increased tracing verbosity for rollout controller and routing translator.
Notified impacted customers and coordinated with customer success for remediation notes.
action_items: Liam Chen - Implement controller-side assert to refuse gate evaluation if region-overrides checksum != rollout-config checksum; PR: runtime#2345; due 2026-03-21
Priya Nair - Backfill unit+integration tests that simulate pinned-session rollback path with mixed KV-cache formats; ticket ENG-128643; due 2026-03-28
Samir Patel - Add rollout gate decision tracing into alert payloads so runbook includes gate metadata; PR: observability#112; due 2026-03-18
Maya Gupta - Create and run canary test harness for region-override concurrency (synthetic traffic + config race simulation); ticket ENG-128644; due 2026-04-01
Security - Review: Confirm KV-cache format changes go through serialization compatibility checklist before release; owner: Security Team; due 2026-03-25
SRE - Update runbook to include steps for forced-unpin with safety checks and a playbook for partial rollbacks; owner: SRE Team; due 2026-03-20
Product - Adjust rollout UI to surface active override diffs and checksum with a one-click rollback disable; owner: Product Management; due 2026-04-05
notes: We observed that the majority of errors occurred within 5 minutes of the stale override application — recommending stricter atomicity for override updates.
The pinlock behavior is intentional to prevent state corruption for long-lived sessions, but we need an escape hatch with safety checks for cross-version incompatibilities.
Follow-up technical spike scheduled to evaluate a backward-compatible KV-cache encoding strategy (base+versioned headers).
Customer success asked for a post-incident summary to share with enterprise customers who experienced increased latency; PRD draft in Confluence.
